{"candidate":{"author":"08cc5093-0f1c-4924-97ab-b3322510d140","content":"{"claims":[{"evidence":["E3","E8","E10"],"id":"C1","text":"All three spikes passed merged-tree checks; A and B used real processes with fixture Directors, and C used a live broker-backed gpt-6-sol Director."},{"evidence":["E5","E6","E9"],"id":"C2","text":"Live Director proof covers starting from a text brief, waiting on the original Task, and a caller-directed abort with zero releases; forbidden-input rejection occurred live, whereas stale and unauthorized probes were fixture-injected."},{"evidence":["E2","E4","E6","E7"],"id":"C3","text":"The external agent, Quality, capability content, and HTTP release receiver remain fixtures, so their passing checks do not establish live end-to-end behavior."},{"evidence":["E6","E7"],"id":"C4","text":"Remaining gaps include external-agent trust and long-Task polling, narrow Director coverage, limited topology testing, and unbuilt operational work."},{"evidence":["E4","E6","E7"],"id":"C5","text":"The recommended next priority is non-fixture agent-to-release qualification with real Quality and capability content, alongside broader live Director scenarios."}],"kind":"verified_report@1","markdown":"## Live-proven\nAll three spikes passed their pre-registered checks on the merged tree. Spikes A and B exercised real processes with fixture Directors; Spike C exercised a live broker-backed `gpt-6-sol` Director. Live Director evidence covers a text brief starting a run, waiting on the original Task, and one caller-directed abort with zero releases. Code rejected a forbidden input requested by the model; stale and unauthorized probes were fixture-injected, not spontaneous model behavior.\n\n## Fixture-only\nThe external agent is a local fixture, while Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures. Their successful checks are not live end-to-end proof.\n\n## Remaining gaps\nExternal-agent authentication and card attestation, a general directory, and workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks are absent. Live Director coverage is limited to one account, one model, and abort; reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured. Topology proof covers two instances only, with no embedded `create_app()` instance lock or stress testing. Old-build retirement, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling remain out of scope or unbuilt.\n\n## Next priority\nQualify a non-fixture external-agent-to-release path with real Quality and capability content, while expanding live Director decisions and briefs. This is a recommended next test, not an established result.","packet_digest":"4973b5f53a9b4736256b56a886591d61cc2b7988eb0df9bb50a0381baec7172c","question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","revision":"r1","title":"Exomachina prototype qualification: live proof and remaining gaps"}","revision":"r1","sha256":"bde8feda00cd0f321ff8fce9b39eddc845949b1f446f29e83cf24941368d98bd"},"kind":"quality_review_request@1","packet":{"default_question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","items":[{"id":"E1","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L18-L20","text":"- **observed-real** means real processes (harness, A2A, runner, Temporal and, where stated, the live broker);
- **observed-synthetic** means real code against a mock;
- **unit-tested** means an isolated test."},{"id":"E2","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L22-L22","text":"A passing fixture is never counted as live proof."},{"id":"E3","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L30-L32","text":"| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |"},{"id":"E4","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L74-L74","text":"- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture."},{"id":"E5","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L116-L119","text":"| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |"},{"id":"E6","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L135-L140","text":"- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured."},{"id":"E7","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L172-L176","text":"- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt."},{"id":"E8","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L150-L152","text":"| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |"},{"id":"E9","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L154-L156","text":"The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases."},{"id":"E10","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L26-L26","text":"**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:"}],"kind":"evidence_packet@1","packet_id":"exo-qualification-2026-09-23","title":"Qualification evidence for the Exomachina Temporal factory prototype"},"packet_digest":"4973b5f53a9b4736256b56a886591d61cc2b7988eb0df9bb50a0381baec7172c","policy_digest":"80436a3dc67d65ea7c2721730a27a3e118f3d300f5a485e879fe207610cad9ea","question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","revision":"r1"}

All three spikes passed their pre-registered checks on the merged tree. Spikes A and B exercised real processes with fixture Directors; Spike C exercised a live broker-backed `gpt-6-sol` Director. Live Director evidence covers a text brief starting a run, waiting on the original Task, and one caller-directed abort with zero releases. Code rejected a forbidden input requested by the model; stale and unauthorized probes were fixture-injected, not spontaneous model behavior.

## Fixture-only
The external agent is a local fixture, while Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures. Their successful checks are not live end-to-end proof.

## Remaining gaps
External-agent authentication and card attestation, a general directory, and workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks are absent. Live Director coverage is limited to one account, one model, and abort; reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured. Topology proof covers two instances only, with no embedded `create_app()` instance lock or stress testing. Old-build retirement, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling remain out of scope or unbuilt.

## Next priority
Qualify a non-fixture external-agent-to-release path with real Quality and capability content, while expanding live Director decisions and briefs. This is a recommended next test, not an established result.","packet_digest":"4973b5f53a9b4736256b56a886591d61cc2b7988eb0df9bb50a0381baec7172c","question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","revision":"r1","title":"Exomachina prototype qualification: live proof and remaining gaps"}

packet.default_question: What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:

| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:

packet.title: Qualification evidence for the Exomachina Temporal factory prototype

brief.question: What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?

findings.problem: Claims the capability content and HTTP release receiver were validated against live production services, but both remain fixtures. The markdown repeats this contradiction.

packet.default_question: What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

## Fixture-only
Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures. The external agent in spike A was also a local fixture, as was its Director. Passing these checks does not prove a live end-to-end release or a fully live external-agent path.

External-agent authentication and card attestation, a general directory, and workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks remain unbuilt. Live Director evidence covers one account, one model, and abort only; broader brief reliability and autonomous decisions are unmeasured. Topology testing covers two instances without stress testing, and embedded create_app() lacks an instance lock. Old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling also remain unresolved.

## Next priority
Qualify an end-to-end path with real Quality, capability content, and release handling, while testing broader Director briefs and decision types. Continue reporting fixture passes separately from live proof.

Code rejected a forbidden input requested by the model; stale and unauthorized probes were fixture-injected, not spontaneous model behavior.

The external agent is a local fixture, while Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures. Their successful checks are not live end-to-end proof.

findings.statement: All three spikes passed their pre-registered checks on the merged tree. A and B ran with real processes but fixture Directors; C also passed with a live broker-backed gpt-6-sol Director.

The live Director proof covers a text brief starting a run, a wait on the original Task, and one caller-directed abort with zero releases. Code rejected a model-requested forbidden input; stale and unauthorized probes were fixture-injected, not spontaneous model behavior.

Fixture success is not live proof: the external agent, Quality, capability content, and HTTP release receiver remain fixtures. Director coverage is limited to one account, one model, and abort; broader reliability is unmeasured.

Remaining gaps include external-agent authentication and attestation, directory and workflow-level remote polling, topology stress testing and an embedded-app instance lock, plus operational hardening and old-build retirement.

The next priority should be an end-to-end qualification using non-fixture external agents, Quality, capability content, and release, while expanding live Director decisions and briefs. This is a recommendation, not a result established by the packet.

risks.statement: End-to-end production behavior remains unproven: all three spikes passed with real processes, and Spike C used a live broker-backed model, but the external agent, quality and capability content, and release receiver remain fixtures. Prioritize a real-agent-to-release integration test without counting fixture passes as live proof.

External-agent trust and recovery are incomplete: cards lack signing or attestation, remote authentication and a general directory are absent, and workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built. Prioritize authenticated, attested contracts and durable polling.

Live Director evidence is narrow: one account and model, a caller-directed abort, and no measured reliability across broader briefs; several rejection probes were fixture-injected rather than spontaneous model behavior. Expand live scenarios before relying on autonomous decisions.
Multi-instance proof covers only two instances; embedded create_app() lacks an instance lock and stress testing is absent. Exercise concurrent startup and failure recovery before scaling topology.
Operational readiness remains unproven: old-build retirement, contract attestation, hardening, and the memory ceiling are explicitly unbuilt or out of scope.

The live broker-backed Director passed C-1 through C-5 with one account and model: it started a run from a text brief, reached an input-required wait, and accepted one caller-directed abort with zero releases. Some rejection probes were fixture-injected rather than spontaneous model behavior.
Quality, capability content, the release receiver, and the external agent remain fixtures; live proof does not establish autonomous decisions, broader-brief reliability, or release behavior.

Remaining gaps include external-agent authentication and attestation, workflow-level polling of long remote Tasks, broader Director coverage, topology stress testing and an embedded-app instance lock, plus operational hardening and other out-of-scope work.

A prudent next priority is to replace a fixture with an authenticated real integration and qualify the resulting end-to-end path, while expanding Director decision and brief coverage; current evidence cannot support treating fixture passes as live proof.

risks.statement: End-to-end production readiness is unproven: A and B passed with a fixture Director, while Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures. Prioritize a live end-to-end run across these components; fixture passes are not live proof.

Live broker-backed Director proof is narrow: one account, one model, and a caller-directed abort, with broader-brief reliability unmeasured. Prioritize varied live briefs and decision types, including autonomous decisions.

External-agent trust and long-running operation remain gaps: cards lack signing or attestation, remote authentication and a general directory are absent, and workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is unbuilt.
Operational scale is unproven: only two instances were tested, embedded create_app() lacks an instance lock, and stress testing, old-build retirement, and the memory ceiling remain unaddressed.

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

Multi-instance proof covers only two instances; embedded create_app() lacks an instance lock and stress testing is absent. Exercise concurrent startup and failure recovery before scaling topology.
Operational readiness remains unproven: old-build retirement, contract attestation, hardening, and the memory ceiling are explicitly unbuilt or out of scope.

findings.statement: All three spikes passed their checks on the merged tree. A and B exercised real processes with a fixture Director; B also exposed a defect in the unmodified code. Passing fixtures are not live proof.

The live broker-backed Director passed C-1 through C-5 with one account and model: it started a run from a text brief, reached an input-required wait, and accepted one caller-directed abort with zero releases. Some rejection probes were fixture-injected rather than spontaneous model behavior.
Quality, capability content, the release receiver, and the external agent remain fixtures; live proof does not establish autonomous decisions, broader-brief reliability, or release behavior.

Remaining gaps include external-agent authentication and attestation, workflow-level polling of long remote Tasks, broader Director coverage, topology stress testing and an embedded-app instance lock, plus operational hardening and other out-of-scope work.

A prudent next priority is to replace a fixture with an authenticated real integration and qualify the resulting end-to-end path, while expanding Director decision and brief coverage; current evidence cannot support treating fixture passes as live proof.

risks.statement: End-to-end production readiness is unproven: A and B passed with a fixture Director, while Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures. Prioritize a live end-to-end run across these components; fixture passes are not live proof.

Live broker-backed Director proof is narrow: one account, one model, and a caller-directed abort, with broader-brief reliability unmeasured. Prioritize varied live briefs and decision types, including autonomous decisions.

External-agent trust and long-running operation remain gaps: cards lack signing or attestation, remote authentication and a general directory are absent, and workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is unbuilt.
Operational scale is unproven: only two instances were tested, embedded create_app() lacks an instance lock, and stress testing, old-build retirement, and the memory ceiling remain unaddressed.

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

packet.default_question: What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:

| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.

packet.default_question: What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:

A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

## Live-proven
The prior live C run proved a broker-backed Director for the abort route. The packet describes earlier qualification of a broker-backed Director in the C route. That run ended with an abort and no release; it does not establish independent model-backed research or Quality.

## Fixture-only
The earlier Quality and capability content were fixtures, as was the HTTP release receiver. Those earlier fixtures exercised workflow and release wiring under test control. The prior qualification does not turn the Quality reviewer, capability outputs, or HTTP receiver into live independent agents.

## Remaining gaps
The live Director proof covered one account, one model, and abort only. The record still leaves independent agent behavior, remote attestation, and operational hardening for this spike to examine. Evidence from the earlier run covers only its stated account, model, and route.

## Next priority
The next priority is to exercise real research, synthesis, and Quality agents while keeping release labeled as a fixture. Run the report graph with separate research, synthesis, and Quality agent processes, then compare their outputs against the pinned packet. Keep the release receiver explicitly labeled as an HTTP fixture.

Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |

The prior live C run proved a broker-backed Director for the abort route. The packet describes earlier qualification of a broker-backed Director in the C route. That run ended with an abort and no release; it does not establish independent model-backed research or Quality.

## Fixture-only
The earlier Quality and capability content were fixtures, as was the HTTP release receiver. Those earlier fixtures exercised workflow and release wiring under test control. The prior qualification does not turn the Quality reviewer, capability outputs, or HTTP receiver into live independent agents.

## Remaining gaps
The live Director proof covered one account, one model, and abort only. The record still leaves independent agent behavior, remote attestation, and operational hardening for this spike to examine. Evidence from the earlier run covers only its stated account, model, and route.

## Next priority
Unbuilt remote attestation is a remaining gap. Run the report graph with separate research, synthesis, and Quality agent processes, then compare their outputs against the pinned packet. Keep the release receiver explicitly labeled as an HTTP fixture.

packet.default_question: What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:

- **observed-synthetic** means real code against a mock;
- **unit-tested** means an isolated test."},{"id":"E2","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L22-L22","text":"A passing fixture is never counted as live proof."},{"id":"E3","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L30-L32","text":"| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |"},{"id":"E4","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L74-L74","text":"- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture."},{"id":"E5","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L116-L119","text":"| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |"},{"id":"E6","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L135-L140","text":"- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured."},{"id":"E7","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L172-L176","text":"- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt."},{"id":"E8","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L150-L152","text":"| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |"},{"id":"E9","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L154-L156","text":"The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases."},{"id":"E10","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L26-L26","text":"**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:"}],"kind":"evidence_packet@1","packet_id":"exo-qualification-2026-09-23","title":"Qualification evidence for the Exomachina Temporal factory prototype"},"packet_digest":"4973b5f53a9b4736256b56a886591d61cc2b7988eb0df9bb50a0381baec7172c","question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","revision":"r1"}
